text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV 2 — unusual tail latency spike detected for endpoint /v1/generate in us-west-2 (prod). p50 up ~+20ms, p95 up ~+700ms in the last 3m. Alerting on-call.

Sam Nguyen: on it. paging the oncall. Who's currently owning us-west-2?

Maria Lopez: I’m watching metrics — traffic volume steady, error rate minor (0.3% 5xx), but timeouts and client-side retries up. Affected customers: 3 high-traffic tenants showing elevated user-facing latency.

Sam Nguyen: copy. Leo, can you grab host perf counters and kernel logs from the inference pods/hosts? Anya, can you pull a couple of traces showing where time is spent?

Leo Chen: collecting now. Running `ssh inference-uw2-012` then `sudo perf stat -a -e context-switches,cpu-migrations,cycles,instructions -I 1000 sleep 3`. Initial output:```
# perf stat -a ...
1000, context-switches, 1,234,567
1000, cpu-migrations, 12,345
1000, cycles, 9.8e+09
1000, instructions, 1.4e+10
```
Context-switch rate jumped ~3x relative to baseline window. Also seeing a small increase in scheduler latency counters.

Anya Patel: jaeger traces show big queuing on the serving process. Span breakdown for a sample request: `accept -> queue_wait (520ms) -> worker_schedule (70ms) -> inference (60ms)`. Most of the added time is in queue_wait. Link: https://jaeger.internal/redwood/trace/abcd1234

Sam Nguyen: queue_wait spiking suggests CPU scheduling/affinity or kernel-level preemption issues. Any recent infra changes? infra-bot, any deploys or kernel repo patches around 04:00-04:10 UTC?

infra-bot: Recent change: kernel livepatch roll-out to us-west-2 node pool started at 2026-03-15T04:06:10Z. Patch id: lp-2026-0315-sched. Rollout automation reported success on 60% of nodes, pending remainder.

Sam Nguyen: that matches the start of the anomaly window. Leo — can you show `dmesg` or `journalctl -u inference-runtime` for affected hosts?

Leo Chen: pasting trimmed logs from inference-uw2-012:```
Mar 15 04:06:12 inference-uw2-012 kernel: audit: type=1400 audit(1710458772.123:45): apparmor=DENIED ...
Mar 15 04:06:15 inference-uw2-012 kernel: scheduler: throttled tasks detected, cpus 0-7
Mar 15 04:06:16 inference-uw2-012 inference-runtime[2345]: WARN queue: task scheduling delay=512ms
Mar 15 04:07:02 inference-uw2-012 kernel: livepatch: applied lp-2026-0315-sched to kernel 6.4.13-44
```
Couple of hosts show the livepatch applied then consistent schedule warnings.

Maria Lopez: customer-facing metrics: p50 baseline 70ms -> 90ms; p95 baseline 220ms -> 980ms. Throughput (req/s) unchanged. Retries up for some tenants which inflates their observed latency.

Sam Nguyen: mitigation options: (1) roll back livepatch, (2) shift traffic to fallback region (us-east-1) for affected tenants, (3) enable local fallback to smaller model variant to reduce queue contention. Which is lowest risk and fastest?

Leo Chen: rollback patch is fastest if patching automation supports it. I can start a partial rollback on a canary subset of hosts. Command we use:```
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/kpatch/rollback -d '{"patch_id":"lp-2026-0315-sched","hosts":["inference-uw2-012"]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'```
I'll target 3 hosts first.

Anya Patel: for customer impact limiter, we can turn on per-tenant regional-fallback for the three affected tenants in the routing controlplane:```
POST /controlplane/v1/routes/fallback
{"tenants":["tenant-a","tenant-b","tenant-c"],"target_region":"us-east-1"}```
This will route new requests to east while we assess.

Sam Nguyen: okay start both mitigations in parallel: Leo, roll back on 3 canaries. Anya, enable routing fallback for affected tenants. Maria, keep monitoring p95 and customer retries. Ops-oncall will take over continuous monitoring after my handoff in 15m.

ops-oncall: taking watch after 15. Please paste a short incident summary and outstanding actions for handoff.

Sam Nguyen: summary for handoff: `SEV2 - us-west-2 p95 spike due to increased queue_wait on inference hosts post kernel livepatch lp-2026-0315-sched`. Actions: `1) rollback lp on 3 canaries (Leo) 2) enable regional fallback for 3 tenants (Anya) 3) monitor p95/p50 (Maria) 4) collect perf and dmesg for nodes where livepatch applied (Leo) 5) open infra ticket to investigate livepatch interaction (Sam -> infra)`.

Leo Chen: rollback started on canaries at 04:21:03Z. After rollback metrics on those canaries: p95 on routed traffic dropped from ~900ms -> 250ms within 2m. perf counters reverted to baseline context-switch rate.

Maria Lopez: after both mitigations: global p95 trending down from 980ms -> 300ms in 8m, p50 stable ~85-100ms. Customer retries back down. Impacted tenants reporting improvements.

Anya Patel: traces post-mitigation show reduced queue_wait: sample spans now `accept -> queue_wait (60ms) -> worker_schedule (40ms) -> inference (70ms)`. Link: https://jaeger.internal/redwood/trace/abcd5678

Sam Nguyen: hypothesis: livepatch `lp-2026-0315-sched` changed scheduler heuristics or timer granularity causing higher context-switch churn and longer run-queue waits for our tightly-coupled inference worker threads. Evidence: 1) temporal correlation with livepatch rollout, 2) perf counters + dmesg scheduler warnings, 3) rollback on canaries recovered tail latency.

ops-oncall: next steps for RCA: 1) collect full perf traces (perf + ftrace) for 10 affected hosts, 2) capture kernel config + livepatch diff, 3) test livepatch on a staging fleet with similar workload, 4) write RCA doc and change request to hold this patch until validated. I'll own the RCA doc.

Sam Nguyen: noted. Maria — please export the customer impact table (tenant, timeframe, p95 delta, retries) and attach to the RCA. Leo — dump `/proc/interrupts`, `top -H -p <inference-pid>`, and perf script for selected windows and upload to the incident artifacts bucket.

Maria Lopez: exporting now, attaching link: s3://incidents/1951234567/customer-impact.csv

Leo Chen: uploading perf traces and logs: s3://incidents/1951234567/perf-traces.tar.gz. Included host list file.

Anya Patel: I've kicked off a staging test to apply the livepatch against a synthetic load that mirrors production. Test id: staging-test-1951. Will update with results.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-4281: "Investigate scheduling livepatch lp-2026-0315-sched causing inference tail latency". Linked artifacts: s3://incidents/1951234567/* . Assigned to infra-team.

Sam Nguyen: great. I'll close the immediate paging loop. ops-oncall will take ownership for RCA and postmortem. If the rollback shows stable behavior we can schedule rework of the livepatch or patch validation steps. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: Taking ownership. Will post the RCA doc link by EOD and invite infra + eng-runtime to review. Leaving this channel open for follow-ups.

[end of thread]
